title: Functions & arrows
description: Three ways to declare callable code: function declarations, expressions, and arrows — plus how each handles this, default params, and implicit returns.

notes: Arrows do NOT bind their own this — they capture this from the enclosing scope.
Implicit return only works with a single expression body (no braces).
Function declarations are hoisted; expressions and arrows assigned to const are NOT — calling them before assignment throws ReferenceError.

questions.q: Which form is hoisted (callable before its line of code)?
questions.explain: A declaration is hoisted whole, so add is callable above its own line. const-assigned expressions and arrows hoist the BINDING only and it sits in the temporal dead zone — calling early throws ReferenceError, not "is not a function".

questions.q: What does an arrow function do with this?
options: Binds it to the global object
Inherits it lexically from the enclosing scope
Binds it to the first argument
questions.explain: An arrow has no this of its own, so this resolves through the enclosing scope at definition time — which is why arrows are safe as callbacks inside a method and wrong as the method itself. call/bind cannot override it either.

options: arrow with no braces n => n * 2
questions.explain: Dropping the braces makes the body a single expression whose value is returned. Put the braces back and it is a statement body again — n => { n * 2 } returns undefined, the classic silent bug.

questions.q: function greet(name = "world") — what happens when called as greet()?
questions.explain: A default fires when the argument is undefined — whether omitted or passed explicitly as undefined. null does NOT trigger it: greet(null) gives "hi null".

exercises.prompt: Write each form: declaration for add, expression for sub, arrow for mul.
Arrow function with a default param and implicit return of a template literal.

L3.prompt: Write a function `multiply(a, b)` where b defaults to 1. Log `multiply(4, 3)` and `multiply(7)` on the same line separated by a space.
hints: Default parameter goes in the parameter list: b = 1.
